content.value_statement: PDF work often requires separate tools for text, tables, forms, and pages. This skill provides focused Python examples for common local PDF tasks.
actual_capabilities: Extract text from a selected page or every page with pdfplumber.
Detect and print tables from PDF pages.
Merge multiple PDF files with pypdf.
Split a PDF by selecting page ranges.
Fill, validate, and flatten PDF form fields.
Save extracted text and tables as local text or CSV files.
limitations: Scanned PDFs need OCR tools such as pytesseract for reliable text extraction.
Table detection quality depends on the PDF layout.
Examples use fixed local filenames and do not manage cloud storage.
Form support depends on fields embedded in the source PDF.

use_cases.title: Extract report data
use_cases.description: Extract text and tables from a report for review or spreadsheet preparation.

use_cases.title: Prepare completed forms
use_cases.description: Validate field values, fill a PDF form, and flatten it for distribution.

use_cases.title: Organize document pages
use_cases.description: Merge related PDFs or split selected pages into a separate document.

prompt_templates.title: Extract text from one PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the text from document.pdf and save it to output.txt. Report pages with no extractable text.

prompt_templates.title: Export a table
prompt_templates.prompt: Find tables on the first page of report.pdf and save the results as output.csv. Preserve rows where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a form safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect form.pdf fields, validate the supplied name, email, and address, then create filled_form.pdf.

prompt_templates.title: Merge and verify documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge these PDFs in order, save merged.pdf, and confirm the output page count: file1.pdf, file2.pdf, file3.pdf.

output_examples.input: Extract text from a three-page report and save it locally.
output: Creates output.txt with extracted page text.
Reports any page that has no extractable text.

output_examples.input: Fill and flatten a customer form.
output: Creates a non-editable flattened PDF for distribution.
Creates merged.pdf in the requested order.
Closes the PDF merger after writing the file.

best_practices: Keep an unchanged copy of each source PDF before editing it.
Validate form values and field names before generating an output file.
Test extraction and page ranges with a small document first.
anti_patterns: Do not expect text extraction to work reliably on image-only PDFs without OCR.
Do not overwrite an original PDF when creating a filled or flattened version.
Do not assume table detection preserves complex layouts perfectly.

faq.question: Which libraries does this skill use?
faq.answer: Examples use pdfplumber for extraction and pypdf for PDF manipulation and forms.

faq.question: Can it read scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Scanned PDFs usually need OCR. The skill mentions pytesseract as an option.

faq.question: Can it extract every page?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to iterate through all pages and combine extracted text.

faq.question: Can it fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: Yes. The form guide shows field inspection, validation, filling, and flattening.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The examples save fixed output files in the local working directory.

faq.question: Does it upload PDFs to a service?
faq.answer: No. The documented examples process local files and do not include network requests.
